newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU WINS SECOND AS YANKEES POUND INDIANS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU WINS SECOND AS YANKEES POUND INDIANS.

text.p: Japanese rookie Hideki Irabu struggled in the heat Tuesday but again got a lot of runs from his New York Yankee teammates, especially Tino Martinez, to notch his second major-league win in as many starts.
Martinez again hit a three-run homer for Irabu, capping a six-run third inning as the Yankees pounded out a 12-6 win over the Cleveland Indians.
Irabu was tagged for five runs and nine hits over five innings, walked one, struck out four and also balked.
"I thought he was a little tired in the fourth," New York manager Joe Torre said. "Because of the weather it was very tough out there, he was done in the fifth. He toughed it out."

"The weather affected me," Irabu said. "There was a big difference between this game and my first game. I am grateful to my teammates for getting so many runs. Otherwise I don't know how it would have come out.
The Yankees have scored 22 runs in the two games Irabu started and only 12 runs for all the other pitchers in four games since his first start.
Ramiro Mendoza gave up one run and four hits over the final four innings to earn his first major-league save.
Martinez tied a career-best when his belted his 31st homer of the season into the right-field seats, giving the Yankees a 7-1 bulge.
New York batted around in the third and seventh innings -- the third time they batted around twice in the same game this season, two of them in the games Irabu started.
Every New York starter hit safely and eight scored a run.
Charles Nagy (9-6), was reached for eight runs and nine hits over 2 1/3 innings. "I just didn't make the pitches I had to," Nagy said.
Tony Fernandez, Marquis Grissom and Matt Williams homered for Cleveland. Chad Curtis also homered for New York.
In Boston, Melvin Nieves's two-out, two-run homer in the top of the 12th off John Wasdin (3-5) lifted the Detroit Tigers to a 7-5 victory over the Red Sox.
Todd Jones (2-3) got the win in relief.
Damon Easley added a solo homer for Detroit, which bounced back from an 18-4 loss Monday.
Embattled Wil Cordero hit his second homer in two games for the Red Sox, who lost for the fourth time in five games.

Earlier Tuesday, Cordero pledged a donation of $114,754.10 to a local anti-poverty agency as a goodwill gesture in response to his arrest last month on charges of battering his wife. After starting 0-for-12 since his return to the lineup Thursday, Cordero has hits in five of his last nine at-bats.

In Baltimore, Lenny Webster homered and tied a career high with four RBI and Jeffrey Hammonds added three hits, including a solo homer, leading the Orioles to an 8-4 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays.
Webster's 440-foot (135 metres) homer over the centre-field fence was the longest by an Oriole this season and the longest of his life.
Shawn Boskie (5-3) allowed two runs and four hits with a season-high seven strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings to win for the fourth time in five decisions.
Juan Guzman (3-6) took the loss.

In Minnesota, Pat Meares drove in three runs and Brad Radke went seven-plus innings to win his eighth straight start as the Twins defeated the Chicago White Sox 8-4, completing a sweep of their two-game series.

Radke (12-5) held Chicago hitless over the first five innings before Mike Cameron led off the sixth with a bloop single. Radke allowed three runs -- one earned -- and five hits with two walks and three strikeouts.
Jaime Navarro (7-8) took the loss.

In Oakland, Mark McGwire hit his major league-leading 32nd homer and drove in four runs and Matt Stairs hit his third homer in two games as the Athletics held on for an 8-5 victory over the Seattle Mariners.
McGwire hit a solo homer in the first inning, added an RBI groundout in the third and a clutch two-run double in the eighth after Seattle had cut a five-run deficit to 6-5.

In Anaheim, Jason Dickson (10-4) allowed one run over seven innings with eight hits, no walks and three strikeouts and the Angels scored five times in the second to beat the Texas Rangers 6-2 for their season-high eighth straight win.
Dave Hollins went 3-for-4 with an RBI and Jim Leyritz drove in two runs for Anaheim, which pulled to within 1 1/2 games of Seattle for the lead in the American League West.
Rangers starter Ken Hill (5-7) lost for the fifth time in six starts.
Will Clark and Warren Newson hit solo homers for Texas.
In Kansas City, Dave Nilsson belted a pair of solo homers as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Kansas City Royals, 5-2.
Scott Karl (3-10) got his first win in nearly two months.
The Brewers, who have won six of their last seven games, have allowed just 14 runs in that span. Milwaukee, which has won four of its last five road games, is still an A.L. worrst 16-31 on the road.
